Over 2857 ms the CPU was busy 26% and 27 outbound network calls took 568 ms combined.

Of the 574 ms render: load functions 33.2 ms + 389 ms waiting · other 52.5 ms + 10.4 ms waiting · component render 37.2 ms · ogygia transform 21.3 ms · remote functions 0.23 ms + 18.6 ms waiting.

6 calls ran one after another for 298 ms: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/session, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/pricing, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/inventory, timer · rows (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:13), queue.drain, timer · value (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:59). Started together they would cost 99.9 ms — about 199 ms saved. → Start them together (Promise.all) when they are independent; a call that needs an earlier result stays sequential.

16 calls to 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/product/:id — one per item, 131 ms together. → Batch them: one request with the ids (or a bulk endpoint), or fetch the list with its children included.

Biggest CPU consumer: node core (156 ms, 21.3% of busy time).

One render of Root costs 156 ms (21.3% of busy). → Compute the expensive part once (in load, or a per-request cache) and pass the result as a prop, or render it in a deferred hole. show the row ↓

stock.lookup ran 16 times in one render (load (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:77)), 128 ms together, 7.87 ms each. → Once per item is the N+1 shape: batch it (one call for all the ids), or fetch the parent with its children included.

ogygia added 14.4 ms to the render: 51 islands, seed 254 KB, props 125 KB, remote seed 164 B.

The page seed is 254 KB: an island reads $page, so that much of page.data ships to the browser and is serialized on every render. → Read only the keys the island needs (page.data.x, not page.data) so seed shaping trims it, or pass the values as props.

PriceTicker, ProductCard read page.data whole, so every key ships in the seed (254 KB, the biggest is catalog at 225 KB). → Read the keys by name (page.data.catalog, not a spread or a loop over page.data) so seed shaping can drop the rest, or pass the values in as props.

The seed (254 KB) left the JSON lane because of catalog.facets (Map) — devalue writes and revives it several times slower than JSON.parse. → Send that value as a plain string or number (a Date as toISOString(), a Map as an object), or keep it out of page.data.

MegaHeader's props (111 KB) use devalue because of config.updated (Date). → JSON props parse on the fast lane in the browser: pass the value as a string or number, or derive it inside the island.

ProductCard has 48 copies on the page, each waking on visible with its own 80 B of props. → One island around the list hydrates once; or wake: 'interaction' so a copy pays only when touched.

Hole 01d4f0f09349: 2 of 3 requests served from the render cache (maxAge 300s).

1 hole renders fresh on every visit (97f70770dcf8 50.9 ms). → Content that is the same for every visitor for a while can take a maxAge: the endpoint then serves the memo.

In the browser, 3 islands reported hydration: 91.7 ms in all (p50), the slowest ProductCard at 57.9 ms. → The hydrate step itself is slow: fewer elements per island, or split the island so the interactive part is small.

_page renders 48 ProductCard rows per render, 23.4 ms together (0.49 ms each). → The list is the cost, not the row: page it, window it, or defer the part below the fold into a hole. show the row ↓

201 ms of busy time is the profiler itself — a one-time cost when recording starts. Your app did not pay this outside the recording.

Flame graph

Width = time. Click a bar to zoom, click it again to zoom back out. Orange bars are your components.
ogygia/profiler — samples the whole Node process during SSR. Self = time (or memory) inside the function itself. Total = self plus everything it called. Per call = total ÷ how many times it ran (a ×N tag means it ran N times; no tag means once).
